content: Pickled tofu, also known as tofu cheese, preserved tofu, or fermented tofu, is a type of processed tofu commonly used in Chinese cuisine. To produce pickled tofu, cubes of dried tofu are first allowed to air-dry completely under hay. Commercially, pickled tofu is made using firm, dry tofu that has been inoculated with fungal spores from species such as Actinomucor elegans, Mucor racemosus, or Rhizopus. Once the tofu has been fermented, it is soaked in a brine solution. This brine is often enriched with ingredients like Chinese rice wine, vinegar, chili peppers, sesame oil, or a paste made from rice and soybeans. For red pickled tofu, red yeast rice, which is cultivated with the fungus Monascus purpureus, is added to impart its characteristic color. Pickled tofu is typically sold in small glass jars. The texture of pickled tofu is unique and has a mouthfeel that is somewhat similar to certain dairy products. This is due to the breakdown of proteins that occurs during the air-drying and fermentation processes. On its own, pickled tofu does not have a strong odor, but it absorbs the flavors and aromas of the liquid in which it is soaked. Its texture is smooth and firm, resembling a creamy paste, and its taste is often compared to that of blue cheese. In fact, it is sometimes referred to as Chinese cheese in English. When stored in a refrigerator, pickled tofu can be preserved for several years, during which its flavor is thought to mature and improve. Pickled tofu is often used in small quantities to enhance the flavor of stir-fried or braised vegetable dishes, particularly those made with leafy greens such as water spinach. A small amount of the soaking liquid is usually added along with the tofu to these dishes. It is also commonly consumed directly as a condiment, paired with rice or congee. It is worth noting that the Hwang Ryh Shang Company, a major producer of pickled tofu in Taiwan, has been known to mislabel red yeast rice as red date (jujube) on the English ingredient list of its product labels, even though the Chinese ingredient list correctly identifies it as 紅糟 (red yeast rice).
